---
title: "TBR prison: analysis"
date: now
---

Reads the published analysis dataset, `data/tbr_prison.csv`, and produces the report's tables and figures: what the projects did, the number needed to screen (NNS) and number needed to test (NNT), those estimates broken down by screening point, method and population, and a decomposition of the NNS into the three steps of the screening cascade.

Two units of analysis run side by side and are never mixed:

-   **Projects** (N = 35) are the unit of the characteristics table. A project counts once in a row if any of its interventions used that stage, point, method or population, so rows are not mutually exclusive.
-   **Interventions** (N = 67) are the unit of every estimate. A single project contributes up to ten of them.

Three conventions hold throughout:

-   A ratio with a zero denominator and a non-zero numerator is undefined (`Inf`), after Garg et al. (*Lancet Reg Health Southeast Asia* 2022). An intervention that screened people and found no case still counts towards (n) and still contributes its screened count to a pooled denominator; `NA` is reserved for a missing input and for 0/0.
-   A pooled estimate is a ratio of totals, so an intervention counts in proportion to how many people it screened.
-   Quantiles are rounded to the nearest whole person, and range endpoints are rounded up: an NNS of 13.9 means 14 people must be screened to expect one case.

Each section names the files it writes. They all land in `output/` (`TableDescriptive.xlsx`, `estimate_summary.xlsx`, `supplementary_tables.xlsx` and four figures, each written once as a 600 dpi PNG) apart from the project-level roll-up, which goes to `data/tbr_project_details.csv`.

## Setup and derived measures

Imports `data/tbr_prison.csv`, rebuilds the `wave` ordering that the CSV round-trip loses, and derives the ratios the rest of the document works from:

| Measure               | Definition                                                                                             |
|-----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `nns_af`, `nns_bplus` | Number needed to screen: people screened per case diagnosed, all forms and bacteriologically confirmed |
| `nnt_af`, `nnt_bplus` | Number needed to test: people tested per case diagnosed, on the same two case definitions               |
| `pdlfu`               | Pre-diagnosis loss to follow-up: the share of people classified presumptive who were never tested       |

Where more people were tested than were classified presumptive, which is what mass screening does, `pdlfu` would go negative, so it is set to missing; it is also missing wherever either of its two inputs is. Three interventions (the Republic of Moldova, Waves 2 and 4, referral-based by design) recorded no screened population, so the per-intervention NNS runs on 64 of 67. Their NNT is unaffected, because `tested` is recorded for all three.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(rio)
  library(here)
  library(gtsummary)
  library(gt)
  library(openxlsx)
  library(sessioninfo)
})

set.seed(42)
```

```{r}
#| label: import
#| include: false

data_path <- here("data", "tbr_prison.csv")
if (!file.exists(data_path)) stop("Missing published dataset: ", data_path)
master <- import(data_path)
dir.create(here("output"), showWarnings = FALSE)

# Validate the published dataset.
count_vars <- c("screened", "presumptive", "tested", "tb_af", "tb_bplus")
flag_vars <- c(
  paste0("screening_stage_", c("mass_screening", "entry_screening", "referral_screening", "exit_screening")),
  paste0("screening_point_", c("intake", "in_prison", "exit", "post_prison")),
  paste0("screening_methods_", c("symptom", "cxr", "cxr_ai", "risk_factor", "contact_tracing", "hiv")),
  paste0("testing_methods_", c("genexpert", "culture", "tst", "smear")),
  paste0("subpopulation_", c("prisoners", "ex_prisoners", "staff", "staff_family", "prisoner_family"))
)
required_vars <- c("intervention_id", "project_code", "country", "who_region",
                   "year_implemented", "wave", "screening_point", "subpopulation_other",
                   count_vars, flag_vars)
missing_vars <- setdiff(required_vars, names(master))
if (length(missing_vars)) stop("Missing analysis columns: ", paste(missing_vars, collapse = ", "))
stopifnot(
  "expected 67 interventions, 35 projects and 25 countries" =
    nrow(master) == 67L && n_distinct(master$project_code) == 35L && n_distinct(master$country) == 25L,
  "intervention identifiers must be unique and complete" =
    !anyNA(master$intervention_id) && all(nzchar(master$intervention_id)) &&
    !anyDuplicated(master$intervention_id),
  "project identifiers and countries must be complete" =
    !anyNA(master$project_code) && all(nzchar(master$project_code)) &&
    !anyNA(master$country) && all(nzchar(master$country)),
  "counts must be numeric, non-negative whole numbers or missing" =
    all(vapply(master[count_vars], function(x) is.numeric(x) &&
      all(is.na(x) | (is.finite(x) & x >= 0 & x == trunc(x))), logical(1))),
  "indicator columns must contain only 0, 1 or missing values" =
    all(vapply(master[flag_vars], function(x) all(is.na(x) | x %in% c(0, 1)), logical(1)))
)

# wave comes back as text from the CSV; restore the numeric ordering.
wave_numbers <- sort(unique(as.integer(str_match(master$wave, "^Wave (\\d+)$")[, 2])))
master <- master %>%
  mutate(wave = factor(wave, levels = paste("Wave", wave_numbers)))
stopifnot("wave failed to parse" = !any(is.na(master$wave)))
```

```{r}
#| label: calculation
#| include: false

# Garg et al. (Lancet Reg Health Southeast Asia 2022): a zero denominator with a
# non-zero numerator is undefined (Inf), not missing. NA is a missing input or 0/0.
count_ratio <- function(numerator, denominator) {
  out <- numerator / denominator
  out[is.na(numerator) | is.na(denominator) | is.nan(out)] <- NA_real_
  out
}

# The three Republic of Moldova interventions have no screened count (referral-based), so
# per-intervention NNS runs on 64 of 67. Their NNT is unaffected.
master <- master %>%
  mutate(
    nns_af    = count_ratio(screened, tb_af),
    nns_bplus = count_ratio(screened, tb_bplus),
    nnt_af    = count_ratio(tested,   tb_af),
    nnt_bplus = count_ratio(tested,   tb_bplus),
    # Pre-diagnosis loss to follow-up; negative (tested > presumptive) is missing.
    pdlfu = 1 - (tested / presumptive),
    pdlfu = if_else(is.nan(pdlfu) | pdlfu < 0, NA_real_, pdlfu)
  )

# The cascade set below additionally needs a presumptive count and has 61 rows.
stopifnot(
  "per-intervention NNS does not run on 64 of 67 interventions" =
    sum(!is.na(master$nns_af)) == 64
)
```

## Project characteristics

Rolls the 67 interventions up to their 35 projects (a flag is "Yes" if any of a project's interventions used it and "No" if none did), then tabulates screening stage, screening point, screening method, testing method and population. This is Table 1 of the manuscript.

Rows within a block are not mutually exclusive and do not sum to 35 or to 100%. Every block has a denominator of 35: the one project whose Subpopulation Detail cell read "N/A" is coded as PDL in the analysis dataset based on the source report.

Writes `data/tbr_project_details.csv` and `output/TableDescriptive.xlsx`.

```{r}
#| label: project-level-details
#| include: false

binary_vars <- c(
  "screening_stage_mass_screening",
  "screening_stage_entry_screening",
  "screening_stage_referral_screening",
  "screening_stage_exit_screening",
  "screening_point_intake",
  "screening_point_in_prison",
  "screening_point_exit",
  "screening_point_post_prison",
  "screening_methods_symptom",
  "screening_methods_cxr",
  "screening_methods_cxr_ai",
  "screening_methods_risk_factor",
  "screening_methods_contact_tracing",
  "screening_methods_hiv",
  "testing_methods_genexpert",
  "testing_methods_culture",
  "testing_methods_tst",
  "testing_methods_smear",
  "subpopulation_prisoners",
  "subpopulation_ex_prisoners",
  "subpopulation_staff",
  "subpopulation_staff_family",
  "subpopulation_prisoner_family"
)

# "Yes" if any intervention used it, "No" if none did, NA if never recorded.
any_yes <- function(x) {
  if (all(is.na(x))) NA_character_ else if (any(x == 1, na.rm = TRUE)) "Yes" else "No"
}

# first() collapses these to one value per project; assert they are constant.
collapsed_vars <- c("country", "who_region", "wave", "year_implemented")

constant_check <- master %>%
  group_by(project_code) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(collapsed_vars), ~ n_distinct(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(if_any(all_of(collapsed_vars), ~ .x > 1))
stopifnot(
  "a first()-collapsed variable is not constant within project_code" =
    nrow(constant_check) == 0
)

project_df <- master %>%
  group_by(project_code) %>%
  summarise(
    year_implemented = first(year_implemented),
    country          = first(country),
    who_region       = first(who_region),
    wave             = first(wave),
    # As any_yes: NA when the source text was never recorded.
    subpopulation_other = if (all(is.na(subpopulation_prisoners))) {
      NA_character_
    } else if (any(!is.na(subpopulation_other) & subpopulation_other != "")) {
      "Yes"
    } else {
      "No"
    },
    across(all_of(binary_vars), any_yes),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(c(all_of(binary_vars), subpopulation_other),
                ~ factor(.x, levels = c("No", "Yes"))))

export(project_df, here("data", "tbr_project_details.csv"))
```

```{r}
#| label: project-level-descriptive-table
#| include: true
#| echo: true

# One spec per stacked block. value = ~ "Yes" forces one row per flag.
tbl_specs <- list(
  list(
    header = "Screening Stage",
    labels = list(
      screening_stage_mass_screening     = "Mass screening",
      screening_stage_entry_screening    = "Entry screening",
      screening_stage_referral_screening = "Referral screening",
      screening_stage_exit_screening     = "Exit screening"
    )
  ),
  list(
    header = "Screening Point",
    labels = list(
      screening_point_intake      = "Entry",
      screening_point_in_prison   = "In-prison",
      screening_point_exit        = "Exit",
      screening_point_post_prison = "Post-prison"
    )
  ),
  list(
    header = "Screening Methods",
    labels = list(
      screening_methods_symptom         = "Symptom",
      screening_methods_cxr             = "CXR",
      screening_methods_cxr_ai          = "CXR-AI",
      screening_methods_risk_factor     = "Risk Factor",
      screening_methods_contact_tracing = "Contact Tracing",
      screening_methods_hiv             = "HIV"
    )
  ),
  list(
    header = "Testing Methods",
    labels = list(
      testing_methods_genexpert = "GeneXpert",
      testing_methods_culture   = "Culture",
      testing_methods_smear     = "Smear"
    )
  ),
  list(
    header = "Subpopulation",
    labels = list(
      subpopulation_prisoners       = "PDL",
      subpopulation_ex_prisoners    = "Ex-PDL",
      subpopulation_staff           = "Staff",
      subpopulation_staff_family    = "Staff Family",
      subpopulation_prisoner_family = "PDL Family",
      subpopulation_other           = "Other"
    )
  )
)

build_block <- function(spec) {
  vars <- names(spec$labels)
  project_df %>%
    tbl_summary(
      include   = all_of(vars),
      label     = spec$labels,
      value     = all_of(vars) ~ "Yes",
      missing   = "no",
      statistic = all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)"
    )
}

table_project_caption <-
  "Characteristics of TB REACH projects conducted in prison from 2011 to 2024"

table_project <- tbl_stack(
  map(tbl_specs, build_block),
  group_header = map_chr(tbl_specs, "header")
) %>%
  # Indent the flag rows under their block headers.
  modify_column_indent(columns = label, rows = tbl_id1 >= 1L, indent = 4L) %>%
  modify_caption(table_project_caption) %>%
  modify_source_note(sprintf(
    paste("Unit of analysis: projects (N = %d). A project counts once in a row if",
          "any of its one or more interventions used that stage, point, method or",
          "population, so rows are not mutually exclusive and do not sum to %d or",
          "to 100%%. The %d projects comprise %d distinct interventions."),
    nrow(project_df), nrow(project_df), nrow(project_df), nrow(master)
  ))

table_project
```

```{r}

table_flat <- gtsummary::as_tibble(table_project) %>%
  rename_with(~ c("group", "characteristic", "n_percent")[seq_along(.x)])

# Use the same XLSX writer as the other exported tables. The pinned openxlsx
# writer emits dangling drawing references and A1-only worksheet dimensions.
rio::export(
  list(TableDescriptive = table_flat, project_details = project_df),
```

```{r}
#| label: project-level-text-numbers
#| include: true
#| echo: true

# PDL "Yes" and every other population flag "No". The Eswatini project counts:
# The analysis dataset codes it as PDL based on the source report.
other_populations <- c("subpopulation_ex_prisoners", "subpopulation_staff",
                       "subpopulation_staff_family", "subpopulation_prisoner_family",
                       "subpopulation_other")
pdl_only <- project_df %>%
  filter(subpopulation_prisoners == "Yes",
         if_all(all_of(other_populations), ~ .x == "No"))

text_numbers <- tibble(
  quantity    = "Projects whose only recorded population is PDL",
  n           = nrow(pdl_only),
  denominator = nrow(project_df),
  percent     = 100 * n / denominator
)

cat(sprintf("%d of %d projects (%.0f%%) screened people deprived of liberty only.\n",
            nrow(pdl_only), nrow(project_df), 100 * nrow(pdl_only) / nrow(project_df)))
```

## Projects by wave

Counts projects, interventions and cascade totals within each TB REACH funding wave. Projects and their main year of implementation (the extraction's `Main Year Implemented` field; the separate range field is not used) come from `project_df`; interventions and counts from `master`. This is Table S1 of the manuscript. The three referral-based interventions (Republic of Moldova, Waves 2 and 4) have no screened count and contribute to the diagnosed columns only.

The table is exported with the other supplementary tables further down.

```{r}
#| label: wave-table
#| include: true
#| echo: true

# Min–max of the projects' main implementation years ("2011–2012", or "2012"
# when they coincide); the extraction's separate range field is not used. Blank
# years are ignored.
year_range <- function(y) {
  y <- y[!is.na(y)]
  if (length(y) == 0) return(NA_character_)
  if (min(y) == max(y)) as.character(min(y)) else paste0(min(y), "–", max(y))
}

wave_projects <- project_df %>%
  group_by(wave) %>%
  summarise(projects = n(),
            years    = year_range(year_implemented),
            .groups  = "drop")

wave_interventions <- master %>%
  group_by(wave) %>%
  summarise(
    interventions = n(),
    n_no_screened = sum(is.na(screened)),
    screened      = sum(screened, na.rm = TRUE),
    tb_af         = sum(tb_af, na.rm = TRUE),
    tb_bplus      = sum(tb_bplus, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups       = "drop"
  )

table_s1_data <- wave_projects %>%
  full_join(wave_interventions, by = "wave") %>%
  arrange(wave)

stopifnot(
  "a wave has projects but no interventions, or the reverse" =
    !any(is.na(table_s1_data$projects) | is.na(table_s1_data$interventions)),
  "the wave table does not account for every project and intervention" =
    sum(table_s1_data$projects) == nrow(project_df) &&
    sum(table_s1_data$interventions) == nrow(master),
  "the screened total by wave differs from the pooled denominator" =
    sum(table_s1_data$screened) == sum(master$screened, na.rm = TRUE),
  "the interventions without a screened count are not the three expected" =
    sum(table_s1_data$n_no_screened) == 3
)

table_s1 <- table_s1_data %>%
  transmute(
    Wave                           = as.character(wave),
    `Main year of implementation`  = years,
    Projects                       = projects,
    Interventions                  = interventions,
    `People screened`              = screened,
    `People diagnosed (all forms)` = tb_af,
    `People diagnosed (B+)`        = tb_bplus
  )

table_s1 <- bind_rows(
  table_s1,
  summarise(table_s1,
            Wave                = "Total",
            `Main year of implementation` = year_range(project_df$year_implemented),
            across(where(is.numeric), sum))
)

no_screened <- master %>%
  filter(is.na(screened)) %>%
  distinct(country, wave) %>%
  mutate(label = sprintf("%s, %s", country, wave)) %>%
  pull(label)

table_s1_note <- sprintf(
  "Three interventions (%s) were referral-based and recorded no screened count; they contribute to the diagnosed columns only.",
  paste(no_screened, collapse = "; ")
)

table_s1 %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "TB REACH projects that screened people deprived of liberty, by funding wave") %>%
  fmt_integer(columns = where(is.numeric)) %>%
  tab_footnote(table_s1_note, locations = cells_column_labels(`People screened`)) %>%
  tab_source_note("Projects and their main year of implementation, as extracted, are counted per project; the remaining columns sum over interventions. B+ = bacteriologically confirmed.")
```

## Headline estimates

Defines the display and summary helpers used from here on, then reports NNS, NNT and pre-diagnosis loss to follow-up two ways in a single table: the per-intervention distribution (median, IQR, observed range) and the pooled estimate (total screened divided by total cases) with a 95% confidence interval.

The interval is a Wilson score interval on the underlying yield (cases per person screened) inverted end-for-end onto the NNS scale, so the lower NNS bound comes from the upper yield bound.

The two counts on the face of the table differ on purpose. The per-intervention (n) is the number of interventions carrying a value; the pooled (n) is the number carrying both counts, which is 64 of 67. The screened and case totals that the pooled ratio actually used are printed alongside them, so the denominator is never implicit.

```{r}
#| label: summary-functions
#| include: false

# NA rather than -Inf/Inf on an all-missing vector. A real Inf passes through.
safe_min <- function(x) if (all(is.na(x))) NA_real_ else min(x, na.rm = TRUE)
safe_max <- function(x) if (all(is.na(x))) NA_real_ else max(x, na.rm = TRUE)

# Integer display. Quantiles to the nearest integer; range endpoints rounded up
# (an NNS of 13.9 means 14 people). Inf prints as "undefined".
disp <- function(x, rounder) {
  out <- rep(NA_character_, length(x))
  finite <- !is.na(x) & is.finite(x)
  out[finite] <- formatC(rounder(x[finite]), format = "d", big.mark = ",")
  out[!is.na(x) & is.infinite(x)] <- "undefined"
  out
}
disp_quantile <- function(x) disp(x, round)
disp_range    <- function(x) disp(x, ceiling)

# Count and proportion display. NA stays NA so gt's sub_missing() can print a dash.
n_fmt <- function(x) {
  out <- rep(NA_character_, length(x))
  ok <- !is.na(x)
  out[ok] <- formatC(x[ok], format = "d", big.mark = ",")
  out
}
pct_fmt <- function(x, digits = 1) {
  out <- rep(NA_character_, length(x))
  ok <- !is.na(x)
  out[ok] <- sprintf("%.*f%%", digits, 100 * x[ok])
  out
}

# Per-intervention distributional summary. n_undefined counts the Inf values.
estimate <- function(data, var, integer_display = TRUE) {
  var <- enquo(var)
  data %>%
    summarize(
      Variable      = quo_name(var),
      Median        = median(!!var, na.rm = TRUE),
      IQR           = IQR(!!var, na.rm = TRUE),
      Q1            = quantile(!!var, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
      Q3            = quantile(!!var, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
      Low           = safe_min(!!var),
      High          = safe_max(!!var),
      n_non_missing = sum(!is.na(!!var)),
      n_missing     = sum(is.na(!!var)),
      n_undefined   = sum(is.infinite(!!var)),
      count         = n(),
      .groups       = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      # pdlfu is a proportion, not a count.
      Median_display = if (integer_display) disp_quantile(Median) else NA_character_,
      Q1_display     = if (integer_display) disp_quantile(Q1)     else NA_character_,
      Q3_display     = if (integer_display) disp_quantile(Q3)     else NA_character_,
      Range_display  = if (integer_display) {
        paste0(disp_range(Low), "–", disp_range(High))
      } else NA_character_
    )
}

# Total screened / total cases over interventions with both recorded, so a
# zero-case intervention still contributes its screened count. Inf when the
# stratum found no case; NA when there is nothing to pool.
pooled_nns <- function(screened, cases) {
  ok <- !is.na(screened) & !is.na(cases)
  if (!any(ok)) return(NA_real_)
  if (sum(screened[ok]) == 0 && sum(cases[ok]) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  if (sum(cases[ok]) == 0) return(Inf)
  ceiling(sum(screened[ok]) / sum(cases[ok]))
}

# Wilson score interval on cases / screened (prop.test without correction),
# inverted onto the NNS scale.
pooled_nns_ci <- function(screened, cases) {
  ok <- !is.na(screened) & !is.na(cases)
  n <- sum(screened[ok]); x <- sum(cases[ok])
  if (!any(ok) || n == 0 || x == 0) return(c(NA_real_, NA_real_))
  ci <- stats::prop.test(x, n, correct = FALSE)$conf.int
  c(ceiling(1 / ci[2]), ceiling(1 / ci[1]))   # invert: upper yield -> lower NNS
}

# Pooled estimate, CI and observed range for one grouping variable and one case
# definition. The pooled set (both counts recorded) is usually smaller than (n),
# so n_complete_pairs, screened_total and cases_total are reported alongside.
estimate_weighted <- function(data, vars, numerators) {
  map_dfr(names(numerators), function(nns_var) {
    cases_col <- numerators[[nns_var]]
    map_dfr(vars, function(var) {
      data %>%
        filter(!is.na(.data[[var]])) %>%
        group_by(option_name = as.character(.data[[var]])) %>%
        summarise(
          WeightedInvMean = pooled_nns(screened, .data[[cases_col]]),
          CI_low          = pooled_nns_ci(screened, .data[[cases_col]])[1],
          CI_high         = pooled_nns_ci(screened, .data[[cases_col]])[2],
          Low             = safe_min(.data[[nns_var]]),
          High            = safe_max(.data[[nns_var]]),
          n_non_missing   = sum(!is.na(.data[[nns_var]])),
          n_missing       = sum(is.na(.data[[nns_var]])),
          n_undefined     = sum(is.infinite(.data[[nns_var]])),
          count           = n(),
          n_total             = n(),
          n_complete_pairs    = sum(!is.na(screened) & !is.na(.data[[cases_col]])),
          n_zero_cases        = sum(.data[[cases_col]] %in% 0),
          n_missing_screened  = sum(is.na(screened)),
          screened_total      = sum(screened[!is.na(screened) & !is.na(.data[[cases_col]])]),
          cases_total         = sum(.data[[cases_col]][!is.na(screened) & !is.na(.data[[cases_col]])]),
          .groups         = "drop"
        ) %>%
        mutate(numerator = nns_var, variable = var, .before = 1)
    })
  })
}
```

```{r}
#| label: estimate-tables
#| include: true
#| echo: true

pdlfu_NA        <- master %>% filter(is.na(pdlfu))
pdlfu_morethan0 <- master %>% filter(!is.na(pdlfu), pdlfu != 0)

# People classified presumptive who were never tested, summed over the
# interventions where the dropout is defined (both counts recorded and tested
# not above presumptive). The mass-testing designs, which tested more people
# than they flagged, are outside this denominator by construction.
pdlfu_defined <- master %>% filter(!is.na(pdlfu))
text_numbers <- bind_rows(
  text_numbers,
  tibble(
    quantity    = sprintf("People classified presumptive who were never tested (%d interventions with a defined dropout)",
                          nrow(pdlfu_defined)),
    n           = sum(pdlfu_defined$presumptive - pdlfu_defined$tested),
    denominator = sum(pdlfu_defined$presumptive),
    percent     = 100 * n / denominator
  )
)

# Overall pooled NNS with the denominator it actually used.
pooled_overall <- tibble(
  Variable  = c("nns_af_wt", "nns_bplus_wt"),
  cases_col = c("tb_af", "tb_bplus"),
  nns_col   = c("nns_af", "nns_bplus")
) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    WeightedInvMean    = pooled_nns(master$screened, master[[cases_col]]),
    CI_low             = pooled_nns_ci(master$screened, master[[cases_col]])[1],
    CI_high            = pooled_nns_ci(master$screened, master[[cases_col]])[2],
    Low                = safe_min(master[[nns_col]]),
    High               = safe_max(master[[nns_col]]),
    n_non_missing      = sum(!is.na(master[[nns_col]])),
    n_missing          = sum(is.na(master[[nns_col]])),
    n_undefined        = sum(is.infinite(master[[nns_col]])),
    count              = nrow(master),
    n_total            = nrow(master),
    n_complete_pairs   = sum(!is.na(master$screened) & !is.na(master[[cases_col]])),
    n_zero_cases       = sum(master[[cases_col]] %in% 0),
    n_missing_screened = sum(is.na(master$screened)),
    screened_total     = sum(master$screened[!is.na(master$screened) & !is.na(master[[cases_col]])]),
    cases_total        = sum(master[[cases_col]][!is.na(master$screened) & !is.na(master[[cases_col]])])
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-cases_col, -nns_col) %>%
  mutate(Range_display = paste0(disp_range(Low), "–", disp_range(High)))

estimate_summary <- bind_rows(
  estimate(master, pdlfu, integer_display = FALSE),
  estimate(master, nnt_af),
  estimate(master, nnt_bplus),
  estimate(master, nns_af),
  estimate(master, nns_bplus)
) %>%
  bind_rows(pooled_overall)

# Presentation copy; estimate_summary stays numeric for the figures and workbook.
measure_labels <- c(
  pdlfu        = "Pre-diagnosis loss to follow-up",
  nnt_af       = "NNT, all forms",
  nnt_bplus    = "NNT, bacteriologically confirmed",
  nns_af       = "NNS, all forms",
  nns_bplus    = "NNS, bacteriologically confirmed",
  nns_af_wt    = "NNS, all forms",
  nns_bplus_wt = "NNS, bacteriologically confirmed"
)

estimate_display <- estimate_summary %>%
  mutate(
    is_pooled = str_detect(Variable, "_wt$"),
    is_prop   = Variable == "pdlfu",
    Block = if_else(
      is_pooled,
      "Pooled across interventions (ratio of totals)",
      "Per-intervention distribution"
    ),
    Measure = unname(measure_labels[Variable]),
    # A pooled n is the number with both counts recorded.
    n_shown = if_else(is_pooled, n_complete_pairs, n_non_missing),
    `Median (IQR)` = case_when(
      is_pooled ~ NA_character_,
      is_prop   ~ sprintf("%s (%s–%s)", pct_fmt(Median), pct_fmt(Q1), pct_fmt(Q3)),
      TRUE      ~ sprintf("%s (%s–%s)", Median_display, Q1_display, Q3_display)
    ),
    `Observed range` = if_else(
      is_prop,
      sprintf("%s–%s", pct_fmt(Low), pct_fmt(High)),
      Range_display
    ),
    `Pooled estimate (95% CI)` = if_else(
      is.na(WeightedInvMean), NA_character_,
      sprintf("%s (%s–%s)", disp_range(WeightedInvMean),
              n_fmt(CI_low), n_fmt(CI_high))
    ),
    Screened = n_fmt(screened_total),
    Cases    = n_fmt(cases_total)
  ) %>%
  select(Block, Measure, n = n_shown, Undefined = n_undefined,
         `Median (IQR)`, `Observed range`, `Pooled estimate (95% CI)`,
         Screened, Cases)

stopifnot("a measure has no display label" = !any(is.na(estimate_display$Measure)))

table_estimates <- estimate_display %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "Block", rowname_col = "Measure") %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Number needed to screen, number needed to test, and pre-diagnosis loss to follow-up"
  ) %>%
  cols_align("center", columns = -c(n, Undefined)) %>%
  cols_align("right", columns = c(n, Undefined)) %>%
  sub_missing(columns = everything(), missing_text = "—") %>%
  tab_footnote(
    "Interventions contributing. For a pooled estimate this is the number with both a screened count and a case count recorded, which is 64 of 67: three interventions were referral-based and screened no population.",
    locations = cells_column_labels(n)
  ) %>%
  tab_footnote(
    "Interventions that screened people and found no one with TB. Their ratio is undefined rather than missing, so they are counted here and kept in every summary.",
    locations = cells_column_labels(Undefined)
  ) %>%
  tab_footnote(
    "Median and interquartile range (Q1–Q3), rounded to the nearest whole person. Pre-diagnosis loss to follow-up is a proportion of those classified presumptive and is shown as a percentage to one decimal place.",
    locations = cells_column_labels(`Median (IQR)`)
  ) %>%
  tab_footnote(
    "Smallest and largest per-intervention value, rounded up: an NNS of 13.9 means 14 people must be screened to expect one case. \"undefined\" is the upper end of a range that contains an intervention that found no one with TB.",
    locations = cells_column_labels(`Observed range`)
  ) %>%

    locations = cells_column_labels(`Pooled estimate (95% CI)`)

    nrow(master), nrow(project_df)
```

## Estimates by screening point, method and population

Recodes screening point onto a single ordered factor and composes combination labels for screening method and population out of the underlying flags, so an intervention that used both symptom screening and chest X-ray reads as "Symptom, CXR" and enters the table once.

The pooled NNS is then computed within each option of the three groupings, for both case definitions side by side. Screening point, method and population are recorded per intervention and are not mutually exclusive across groupings, so an intervention appears once in each of the three blocks and the blocks are not additive.

```{r}
#| label: new-categories
#| include: false

n_missing_point_before <- sum(is.na(master$screening_point))

master <- master %>%
  mutate(
    screening_point = recode(
      screening_point,
      "In-prison"                        = "In Prison",
      "Intake"                           = "Entry",
      "Exit"                             = "Exit",
      "Post-prison"                      = "Post Prison",
      "Detention-associated environment" = "Detention Associated Environment",
      "Intake, In-prison"                = "Entry; In Prison",
      "Intake and In-prison"             = "Entry; In Prison",
      "In-prison, Post-prison"           = "In Prison; Post Prison",
      "Intake, In-prison, Exit"          = "Entry; In Prison; Exit"
    ),
    screening_point = factor(
      screening_point,
      levels = c(
        "Entry", "In Prison", "Exit", "Post Prison",
        "Detention Associated Environment", "Entry; In Prison",
        "In Prison; Post Prison", "Entry; In Prison; Exit"
      )
    )
  )

# A value not covered by the recode would become NA and drop out silently.
stopifnot(
  "a screening_point value is not covered by the recode/factor levels" =
    sum(is.na(master$screening_point)) == n_missing_point_before
)

# Combination label from 0/1 flags. NA flags count as not used; all-zero gives NA.
combine_flags <- function(df, cols, labels) {
  m <- as.matrix(df[cols])
  m[is.na(m)] <- 0
  out <- apply(m, 1, function(r) paste(labels[r == 1], collapse = ", "))
  na_if(out, "")
}

master <- master %>%
  mutate(
    cxr = pmax(screening_methods_cxr, screening_methods_cxr_ai, na.rm = TRUE),
    other_ind = if_else(
      !is.na(subpopulation_other) &
        !(str_trim(as.character(subpopulation_other)) %in% c("", "0")),
      1L, 0L
    )
  )

master$screening_method <- combine_flags(
  master,
  c("screening_methods_symptom", "cxr", "screening_methods_risk_factor",
    "screening_methods_contact_tracing", "screening_methods_hiv"),
  c("Symptom", "CXR", "Risk factor", "Contact tracing", "HIV")
)

master$subpopulation <- combine_flags(
  master,
  c("subpopulation_prisoners", "subpopulation_ex_prisoners",
    "subpopulation_staff", "subpopulation_staff_family",
    "subpopulation_prisoner_family", "other_ind"),
  c("PDL", "Ex-PDL", "Staff", "Staff family", "PDL family", "Other")
)

# Singles first, then combinations by number of components.
method_levels <- master %>%
  distinct(screening_method) %>%
  filter(!is.na(screening_method)) %>%
  arrange(str_count(screening_method, ","), screening_method) %>%
  pull(screening_method)

single_levels <- c("PDL", "Ex-PDL", "Staff", "Staff family", "PDL family", "Other")

master <- master %>%
  mutate(
    screening_method = factor(screening_method, levels = method_levels),
    subpopulation    = factor(subpopulation),
    # Only the singles that occur; naming an absent level warns.
    subpopulation    = fct_relevel(
      subpopulation,
      intersect(single_levels, levels(subpopulation)),
      after = 0
    )
  )
```

### Screening method by testing method

Cross-tabulates the screening-method combination against the testing-method combination at the intervention level (N = 67), as Table S3 of the manuscript. The testing combination is built with the same `combine_flags()` over sputum smear microscopy, GeneXpert and culture. One intervention (Brazil, Wave 4) recorded no testing method and is shown as "Not recorded". Tuberculin skin testing is left out because it tests for infection, not disease.

```{r}
#| label: methods-crosstab
#| include: true
#| echo: true

master$testing_method <- combine_flags(
  master,
  c("testing_methods_smear", "testing_methods_genexpert", "testing_methods_culture"),
  c("Smear", "Xpert", "Culture")
)

# Singles first, then combinations; "Not recorded" last.
testing_levels <- master %>%
  distinct(testing_method) %>%
  filter(!is.na(testing_method)) %>%
  arrange(str_count(testing_method, ","), testing_method) %>%
  pull(testing_method)

master <- master %>%
  mutate(testing_method = factor(replace_na(testing_method, "Not recorded"),

stopifnot(
  "every intervention should have a screening-method combination" =
    !any(is.na(master$screening_method)),
  "expected exactly one intervention without a recorded testing method" =
    sum(master$testing_method == "Not recorded") == 1

table_s3 <- bind_rows(

stopifnot(
  "the cross-tabulation does not account for every intervention" =
    table_s3$Total[table_s3$`Screening method` == "Total"] == nrow(master)
)

table_s3 %>%
  gt(rowname_col = "Screening method") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Screening method by testing method, number of interventions") %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "Testing method", columns = -Total) %>%
  tab_source_note("Unit of analysis: interventions (N = 67). A combination lists every method the intervention used.")
```

```{r}
#| label: weighted-estimates
#| include: true
#| echo: true

weighted_summary <- estimate_weighted(
  master,
  vars       = c("screening_point", "screening_method", "subpopulation"),
  numerators = list(nns_af = "tb_af", nns_bplus = "tb_bplus")
)

data_labeled <- weighted_summary %>%
  mutate(
    variable = factor(variable,
                      levels = c("screening_point", "screening_method", "subpopulation"),
                      labels = c("Screening point", "Screening method", "Subpopulation")),
    # Range endpoints rounded up; a zero-case group prints "undefined" as its maximum.
    pooled_display = disp_range(WeightedInvMean),
    est.lab = case_when(
      is.na(WeightedInvMean)   ~ NA_character_,
      count == 1               ~ pooled_display,
      is.na(Low) | is.na(High) ~ pooled_display,

                     disp_range(Low), disp_range(High))
    ),
    # est.lab with an en dash, for the figure.
    est_fig = case_when(
      is.na(WeightedInvMean)   ~ NA_character_,
      count == 1               ~ pooled_display,
      is.na(Low) | is.na(High) ~ pooled_display,
      TRUE ~ sprintf("%s (%s–%s)", pooled_display,
                     disp_range(Low), disp_range(High))
    ),
    # n on the figure counts the interventions that contribute to the point and
    # the bar (a screened count and a case count), not the group's membership.
    option_label = sprintf("%s (n=%d)", option_name, n_non_missing)
  )

# One row per option, both case definitions side by side, in factor-level order.
group_vars <- c("Screening point"  = "screening_point",
                "Screening method" = "screening_method",
                "Subpopulation"    = "subpopulation")

option_order <- imap_dfr(group_vars, function(raw, lab) {
  tibble(variable     = lab,
         option_name  = levels(master[[raw]]),
         option_order = seq_along(levels(master[[raw]])))
})

# An option that is not a level of its source factor would sort to the end.
stopifnot(
  "an option in the estimates is not a level of its source factor" =
    nrow(anti_join(
      distinct(mutate(data_labeled, variable = as.character(variable)),
               variable, option_name),
      option_order, by = c("variable", "option_name")
    )) == 0
)

pooled_long <- data_labeled %>%
  mutate(
    variable   = as.character(variable),
    pooled_ci  = if_else(
      is.na(WeightedInvMean), NA_character_,
      sprintf("%s (%s–%s)", disp_range(WeightedInvMean),
              n_fmt(CI_low), n_fmt(CI_high))

    arm        = if_else(numerator == "nns_af", "af", "bplus")

         arm, pooled_ci, range_disp)

# screened does not depend on the case definition, so it is carried as an id column.
stopifnot(
  "the screened denominator differs by case definition" =
    pooled_long %>%
      group_by(variable, option_name) %>%

)

pooled_group_display <- pooled_long %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from  = arm,

  left_join(option_order, by = c("variable", "option_name")) %>%
  arrange(match(variable, names(group_vars)), option_order) %>%

    Option     = option_name,

    Screened   = n_fmt(screened_total),

table_pooled <- pooled_group_display %>%
```

## Three-level random-effects model

A sensitivity analysis for the pooled NNS. The pooled ratio counts every intervention in proportion to how many people it screened, so the largest interventions dominate it, and its Wilson interval carries only binomial sampling error. The three-level random-effects model is a binomial generalised linear mixed model (`lme4::glmer`, Laplace approximation) with random intercepts for project and for intervention within project: it models the binomial counts while allowing variation between projects and between interventions within projects. Its NNS is `1 / plogis(fixed intercept)`, the inverse yield at zero project and intervention random effects, rather than a yield averaged over the random-effects distribution. The 95% Wald CI for the fixed intercept is transformed to yield, inverted end-for-end and rounded up like every other NNS in this document. See the [lme4 model documentation](https://lme4.github.io/lme4/reference/glmer.html) for the conditional mean and Laplace approximation. Fitted on the 64 interventions with a screened count (32 projects); an intervention that found no one with TB contributes its screened count without a continuity correction.

Table S2 of the manuscript sets the per-intervention distribution, the pooled NNS and the random-effects NNS side by side, with the two variance components.

```{r}
#| label: random-effects
#| include: true
#| echo: true

library(lme4)

re_data <- master %>%
  filter(!is.na(screened), screened > 0) %>%
  mutate(project_code = factor(project_code), intervention_id = factor(intervention_id))

stopifnot(
  "the random-effects set is not the 64 interventions from 32 projects" =
    nrow(re_data) == 64 && n_distinct(re_data$project_code) == 32
)

fit_three_level <- function(cases_col) {
  d <- re_data %>%
    transmute(project_code, intervention_id, screened, cases = .data[[cases_col]])
  stopifnot("a case count is missing or exceeds the screened count" =
              all(!is.na(d$cases) & d$cases <= d$screened))
  fit <- glmer(cbind(cases, screened - cases) ~ 1 + (1 | project_code / intervention_id),
               data = d, family = binomial, nAGQ = 1L, na.action = na.fail)
  beta <- unname(fixef(fit)[["(Intercept)"]])
  se   <- sqrt(as.numeric(vcov(fit)[1, 1]))
  vc   <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(fit))
  tibble(
    cases_col        = cases_col,
    yield            = plogis(beta),
    nns              = 1 / plogis(beta),
    nns_low          = 1 / plogis(beta + 1.96 * se),   # upper yield -> lower NNS
    nns_high         = 1 / plogis(beta - 1.96 * se),
    var_project      = vc$vcov[vc$grp == "project_code"],
    var_intervention = vc$vcov[vc$grp == "intervention_id:project_code"],
    n                = nrow(d),
    n_projects       = n_distinct(d$project_code),
    converged        = all(fit@optinfo$conv$opt == 0) &&
                         length(fit@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages) == 0,
    singular         = isSingular(fit)
  )
}

re_summary <- bind_rows(fit_three_level("tb_af"), fit_three_level("tb_bplus"))

stopifnot(
  "the three-level model reported a convergence problem" = all(re_summary$converged),
  "the three-level model has a singular fit" = !any(re_summary$singular),
  "a variance component is missing" =
    !any(is.na(re_summary$var_project) | is.na(re_summary$var_intervention))
)

# One column of Table S2: the three estimates and the two variance components.
s2_column <- function(nns_var, wt_var, re_row) {
  per  <- estimate_summary %>% filter(Variable == nns_var)
  pool <- estimate_summary %>% filter(Variable == wt_var)
  stopifnot("Table S2 needs exactly one row per estimate" = nrow(per) == 1 && nrow(pool) == 1)
  c(
    sprintf("%s (%s–%s)", per$Median_display, per$Q1_display, per$Q3_display),
    sprintf("%s (%s–%s)", disp_range(pool$WeightedInvMean), n_fmt(pool$CI_low), n_fmt(pool$CI_high)),
    sprintf("%s (%s–%s)", disp_range(re_row$nns), disp_range(re_row$nns_low), disp_range(re_row$nns_high)),
    sprintf("%.2f", re_row$var_project),
    sprintf("%.2f", re_row$var_intervention)
  )
}

table_s2 <- tibble(
  Estimate = c(
    "Per-intervention NNS, median (IQR)",
    "Pooled NNS, total screened / total diagnosed (95% Wilson CI)",
    "Three-level random-effects NNS (95% CI)",
    "Variance between projects (logit scale)",
    "Variance between interventions within project (logit scale)"
  ),
  `All forms` = s2_column("nns_af", "nns_af_wt", re_summary[re_summary$cases_col == "tb_af", ]),
  `B+`        = s2_column("nns_bplus", "nns_bplus_wt", re_summary[re_summary$cases_col == "tb_bplus", ])
)

table_s2 %>%
  gt(rowname_col = "Estimate") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Number needed to screen: per-intervention, pooled and random-effects estimates") %>%
  tab_source_note(sprintf(
    paste("%d interventions from %d projects with a screened count. The random-effects",
          "estimate is from a binomial generalised linear mixed model with random intercepts",
          "for project and for intervention within project; its NNS is the inverse of the",
          "yield at zero random effects, with an inverted 95%% Wald CI for the fixed intercept. B+ = bacteriologically confirmed."),
    re_summary$n[1], re_summary$n_projects[1]))
```

## Numbers for the Results prose

Collects the quantities the manuscript quotes that are not cells of a table, beyond the two computed with the headline estimates: the interventions with and without a testing dropout, the cascade totals over the 64 interventions with a screened count, the interventions that tested beyond the presumptive group or combined screening points, the range of the breadth of screen, the extremes of the pooled NNS within each grouping of Figures 2 and 3, and the random-effects NNS.

```{r}
#| label: text-numbers-v6
#| include: false

lab_int <- function(d) sprintf("%s (%s)", d$country, d$intervention_id)

# (a) to (c): the testing dropout where it is defined.
dropout_zero <- pdlfu_defined %>% filter(pdlfu == 0)
dropout_some <- pdlfu_defined %>% filter(pdlfu > 0)
dropout_high <- dropout_some %>% filter(pdlfu > 0.30)

# (d) cascade totals over the interventions with a screened count.
screened_set <- master %>% filter(!is.na(screened))

# (e) tested beyond the presumptive group; (f) combined screening points.
tested_beyond   <- master %>% filter(!is.na(presumptive), !is.na(tested), tested > presumptive)
combined_points <- master %>% filter(str_detect(as.character(screening_point), ";"))

# (g) breadth of screen: undefined (Inf) where no one was classified presumptive.
breadth <- screened_set %>%
  filter(!is.na(presumptive)) %>%
  mutate(breadth = count_ratio(screened, presumptive))
breadth_finite    <- breadth %>% filter(is.finite(breadth))
breadth_undefined <- breadth %>% filter(!is.finite(breadth))

# (h) lowest and highest pooled NNS within each grouping of Figures 2 and 3.
nns_extremes <- data_labeled %>%
  filter(is.finite(WeightedInvMean)) %>%
  group_by(numerator, variable) %>%
  slice(c(which.min(WeightedInvMean), which.max(WeightedInvMean))) %>%
  mutate(end = c("Lowest", "Highest")) %>%
  ungroup()

text_numbers <- bind_rows(
  text_numbers,
  tibble(
    quantity    = "Interventions with a defined dropout in which everyone classified presumptive was tested",
    n           = nrow(dropout_zero),
    denominator = nrow(pdlfu_defined),
    percent     = 100 * n / denominator
  ),
  tibble(
    quantity    = "Interventions with a defined dropout in which some people classified presumptive were not tested",
    n           = nrow(dropout_some),
    denominator = nrow(pdlfu_defined),
    percent     = 100 * n / denominator,
    detail      = sprintf("untested share: median %s, IQR %s–%s",
                          pct_fmt(median(dropout_some$pdlfu)),
                          pct_fmt(quantile(dropout_some$pdlfu, 0.25)),
                          pct_fmt(quantile(dropout_some$pdlfu, 0.75)))
  ),
  tibble(
    quantity    = "Interventions in which more than 30% of people classified presumptive were not tested",
    n           = nrow(dropout_high),
    denominator = nrow(pdlfu_defined),
    percent     = 100 * n / denominator,
    detail      = paste(sprintf("%s %s", lab_int(dropout_high), pct_fmt(dropout_high$pdlfu)),
                        collapse = "; ")
  ),
  tibble(
    quantity    = sprintf("People classified presumptive over the %d interventions with a screened count (%d with a presumptive count)",
                          nrow(screened_set), sum(!is.na(screened_set$presumptive))),
    n           = sum(screened_set$presumptive, na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  tibble(
    quantity    = sprintf("People tested over the %d interventions with a screened count (%d with a tested count)",
                          nrow(screened_set), sum(!is.na(screened_set$tested))),
    n           = sum(screened_set$tested, na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  tibble(
    quantity    = "Interventions that tested more people than they classified presumptive",
    n           = nrow(tested_beyond),
    detail      = paste(lab_int(tested_beyond), collapse = "; ")
  ),
  tibble(
    quantity    = "Interventions recorded with a combined screening point",
    n           = nrow(combined_points),
    detail      = paste(sprintf("%s: %s", lab_int(combined_points), combined_points$screening_point),
                        collapse = "; ")
  ),
  tibble(
    quantity    = "Breadth of screen (people screened per person classified presumptive): interventions with a finite value",
    n           = nrow(breadth_finite),
    detail      = sprintf("lowest %.1f (%s), highest %.1f (%s); undefined (no one classified presumptive) in %s",
                          min(breadth_finite$breadth),
                          lab_int(slice_min(breadth_finite, breadth, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)),
                          max(breadth_finite$breadth),
                          lab_int(slice_max(breadth_finite, breadth, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)),
                          paste(lab_int(breadth_undefined), collapse = "; "))
  ),
  nns_extremes %>%
    transmute(
      quantity = sprintf("%s pooled NNS by %s, %s", end, tolower(as.character(variable)),
                         if_else(numerator == "nns_af", "all forms", "bacteriologically confirmed")),
      n        = WeightedInvMean,
      detail   = sprintf("%s (n=%d): 95%% CI %s–%s; screened %s, cases %s",
                         option_name, count, n_fmt(CI_low), n_fmt(CI_high),
                         n_fmt(screened_total), n_fmt(cases_total))
    ),
  re_summary %>%
    transmute(
      quantity = sprintf("Three-level random-effects NNS, %s",
                         if_else(cases_col == "tb_af", "all forms", "bacteriologically confirmed")),
      n        = ceiling(nns),
      detail   = sprintf("95%% CI %s–%s; yield %.3f%%; variance between projects %.2f, between interventions within project %.2f",
                         disp_range(nns_low), disp_range(nns_high), 100 * yield,
                         var_project, var_intervention)
    )
)
```

```{r}
#| label: text-numbers-v8
#| include: false

# (i) The per-intervention median NNS within each option of Figures 2 and 3,
# so the prose can set a pooled contrast beside the typical intervention.
# (j) The largest intervention's share of the people screened in each option,
# which is what carries a pooled contrast when it exceeds a half.
option_long <- master %>%
  select(intervention_id, country, screened, nns_af, nns_bplus,
         screening_point, screening_method, subpopulation) %>%
  mutate(across(c(screening_point, screening_method, subpopulation), as.character)) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(screening_point, screening_method, subpopulation),
               names_to = "variable", values_to = "option_name") %>%
  filter(!is.na(option_name)) %>%
  mutate(variable = str_replace_all(variable, "_", " "))

option_medians <- option_long %>%
  group_by(variable, option_name) %>%
  summarise(
    n_nns        = sum(!is.na(nns_af)),
    median_af    = median(nns_af, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_bplus = median(nns_bplus, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups      = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n_nns > 0)

option_dominance <- option_long %>%
  filter(!is.na(screened)) %>%
  group_by(variable, option_name) %>%
  mutate(share = screened / sum(screened), n_screened = n()) %>%
  slice_max(share, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()

stopifnot(
  "an option has a median but no dominance row, or the reverse" =
    setequal(paste(option_medians$variable, option_medians$option_name),
             paste(option_dominance$variable, option_dominance$option_name))
)

text_numbers <- bind_rows(
  text_numbers,
  option_medians %>%
    transmute(
      quantity = sprintf("Per-intervention median NNS by %s: %s, all forms", variable, option_name),
      n        = median_af,
      detail   = sprintf("median over %d interventions with an NNS; displays as %s", n_nns, disp_quantile(median_af))
    ),
  option_medians %>%
    transmute(
      quantity = sprintf("Per-intervention median NNS by %s: %s, bacteriologically confirmed", variable, option_name),
      n        = median_bplus,
      detail   = sprintf("median over %d interventions with an NNS; displays as %s", n_nns, disp_quantile(median_bplus))
    ),
  option_dominance %>%
    transmute(
      quantity    = sprintf("Largest intervention's share of people screened by %s: %s", variable, option_name),
      n           = screened,
      denominator = round(screened / share),
      percent     = 100 * share,
      detail      = sprintf("%s, %d interventions with a screened count", lab_int(option_dominance)[row_number()], n_screened)
    )
)
```
