## NNS forest figures

One figure per case definition: pooled NNS by screening point, screening method and subpopulation, on a log axis. `Figure_pooled_nns_af` is Figure 2 of the manuscript and `Figure_pooled_nns_bplus` is Figure 3. The title and legend of every figure from here on are held in this document, worded as in the manuscript, so each image file carries the plot alone.

**Figure 2: Pooled number needed to screen (NNS) for all forms of TB.** Forest plot detailing the pooled number needed to screen (NNS) for all forms of TB, disaggregated by screening point (section A), screening method (section B) and subpopulation (section C). Solid points are pooled estimates over the n interventions in each group that recorded both a screened count and a case count. Bars show the observed range of per-intervention values. A bar ending in an arrow has an undefined upper end, because an intervention in that group screened people and found no one with TB.

**Figure 3: Pooled number needed to screen (NNS) for bacteriologically confirmed TB (B+ TB).** Forest plot detailing the pooled number needed to screen (NNS) for bacteriologically confirmed TB (B+ TB), disaggregated by screening point (section A), screening method (section B) and subpopulation (section C). Solid points are pooled estimates over the n interventions in each group that recorded both a screened count and a case count. Bars show the observed range of per-intervention values. A bar ending in an arrow has an undefined upper end, because an intervention in that group screened people and found no one with TB.

Writes `Figure_pooled_nns_af` and `Figure_pooled_nns_bplus` to `output/`.

```{r}
#| label: figures
#| include: true
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 6.26
#| fig-height: 3.85

# The bar is the observed range of per-intervention NNS, not a CI; the point is
# pooled over totals. A zero-case intervention runs its bar off the panel and
# plots no dot.

# Geometry: one 1060 px-wide canvas drawn in a single panel, so a layout px maps
# to a fixed number of mm. 159 mm is the manuscript's A4 text column.
fig_w_mm   <- 159      # A4 text column; 190 for a full-bleed double-column journal
type_scale <- 1.20     # keeps every label at or above 7 pt at 159 mm
CARD_W     <- 1060     # the layout canvas, in layout px

mm_per_px <- fig_w_mm / CARD_W
px  <- function(v) v * mm_per_px                # layout px -> mm (geometry)
tsz <- function(v) v * mm_per_px * type_scale   # layout px -> ggplot text size
# ggplot draws lines and points about 3/4 of the nominal mm value.
lw  <- function(v) px(v) / 0.75
psz <- function(v) px(v) / 0.75

# Helvetica stands in for Source Sans 3. Column widths are measured, not fixed.
fam <- "Helvetica"

pal <- c("Screening point"  = "#8E2F3C",   # maroon
         "Screening method" = "#1F6E73",   # peacock
         "Subpopulation"    = "#A97B23")   # gold
ink <- "#2A2620"; muted <- "#6E6759"; secondary <- "#8A8375"
row_rule <- "#F0EBE1"; gridline <- "#E2DCCE"; legend_dot <- "#555046"

# Axis defaults for all forms (data 14 to 2203); B+ passes its own.
X_LIMITS <- c(12, 2400); X_BREAKS <- c(30, 100, 300, 1000)
PAD <- 10                                  # gutter between text and plot column
H_HEADER <- 22; H_ROW <- 25; GAP_SECTION <- 8
PAD_TOP <- 12; PAD_BOTTOM <- 10; PAD_SIDE <- 16
CONTENT_W <- CARD_W - 2 * PAD_SIDE            # rules and columns sit inside the padding
H_TICKS <- 20; GAP_TITLE <- 6; H_TITLE <- 18
GAP_LEGEND <- 8; H_LEGEND <- 20
LEGEND_N <- c(1, 10, 25, 50)
# 14 layout px = 7.2 pt at print size.
NOTE_PX <- 14

dia_px <- function(n) 4 + 2.1 * sqrt(n)       # mean-marker diameter, layout px

# String width in layout px, measured on the graphics device.
str_w_px <- function(s, size_px) {
  if (length(grDevices::dev.list()) == 0) {
    grDevices::pdf(NULL); on.exit(grDevices::dev.off(), add = TRUE)
  }
  fs <- tsz(size_px) / 0.3528                 # mm -> pt
  vapply(s, function(x) {
    grid::convertWidth(
      grid::grobWidth(grid::textGrob(
        x, gp = grid::gpar(fontfamily = fam, fontsize = fs))),
      "mm", valueOnly = TRUE) / mm_per_px
  }, numeric(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}

# Per-intervention NNS by section and category: the translucent dots.
per_intervention <- master %>%
  select(screening_point, screening_method, subpopulation, nns_af, nns_bplus) %>%
  mutate(across(c(screening_point, screening_method, subpopulation), as.character)) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(screening_point, screening_method, subpopulation),
               names_to = "variable", values_to = "option_name") %>%
  filter(!is.na(option_name)) %>%
  mutate(variable = factor(variable,
                           levels = c("screening_point", "screening_method", "subpopulation"),
                           labels = names(pal)))

nns_figure <- function(which_nns, x_title, x_limits = X_LIMITS, x_breaks = X_BREAKS) {
  X_MIN <- x_limits[1]; X_MAX <- x_limits[2]; BREAKS <- x_breaks
  cats <- data_labeled %>%
    filter(numerator == which_nns) %>%
    group_by(variable) %>%
    arrange(WeightedInvMean, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(rank = row_number()) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(col = unname(pal[as.character(variable)]),
           # n on the figure is the contributing count (a screened count and a
           # case count), not the group's membership; so is the point size.
           n_lab = sprintf("(n=%d)", n_non_missing))
  # Only finite values have an axis position; an undefined range end is drawn
  # to the panel edge, an undefined pooled estimate fails.
  on_axis <- c(cats$WeightedInvMean, cats$Low, cats$High)
  on_axis <- on_axis[is.finite(on_axis)]
  stopifnot(
    "a category has no pooled estimate to plot" = !any(is.na(cats$WeightedInvMean)),
    "a category has an undefined pooled estimate, which cannot be placed on the axis" =
      !any(is.infinite(cats$WeightedInvMean)),
    "a section is missing from the palette"     = !any(is.na(cats$col)),
    "a pooled estimate or range end falls outside the plotted axis" =
      all(on_axis >= X_MIN & on_axis <= X_MAX)
  )

  # Columns sized to the widest string; 288/116 are the floor.
  w_lab <- max(288, ceiling(max(str_w_px(cats$option_label, 15.5))) + 2 * PAD)
  w_est <- max(116, ceiling(max(str_w_px(cats$est_fig, 15))) + 2 * PAD)
  if (w_lab > 288 || w_est > 116) {
    message("figure columns widened for ", fam, ": labels ", w_lab, " px, estimates ", w_est, " px")
  }
  x_lab   <- PAD_SIDE + w_lab - PAD           # labels are right-aligned here
  x_plot0 <- PAD_SIDE + w_lab
  w_plot  <- CONTENT_W - w_lab - w_est
  x_est   <- PAD_SIDE + CONTENT_W - w_est + PAD
  x_of <- function(v) {
    x_plot0 + (log10(v) - log10(X_MIN)) / (log10(X_MAX) - log10(X_MIN)) * w_plot
  }

  # Lay out top-down in layout px, then flip once at the end.
  cursor <- PAD_TOP
  sec <- list(); rows <- list()
  for (s in names(pal)) {
    dd <- filter(cats, variable == s)
    hdr_bottom <- cursor + H_HEADER
    sec[[s]] <- tibble(
      section = s, letter = LETTERS[match(s, names(pal))], col = unname(pal[s]),
      rule_y = hdr_bottom - 1.25, text_y = hdr_bottom - 7,
      rows_top = hdr_bottom, rows_bottom = hdr_bottom + H_ROW * nrow(dd)
    )
    rows[[s]] <- dd %>%
      mutate(y_top = hdr_bottom + (rank - 1) * H_ROW,
             y_mid = y_top + H_ROW / 2,
             y_rule = y_top + H_ROW)
    cursor <- hdr_bottom + H_ROW * nrow(dd) + GAP_SECTION
  }
  sec <- bind_rows(sec); rows <- bind_rows(rows)
  cursor <- cursor - GAP_SECTION                    # no gap after the last section

  ticks_y  <- cursor + 3
  title_y  <- cursor + H_TICKS + GAP_TITLE + H_TITLE / 2
  legend_y <- cursor + H_TICKS + GAP_TITLE + H_TITLE + GAP_LEGEND + H_LEGEND / 2
  total_h  <- cursor + H_TICKS + GAP_TITLE + H_TITLE +
    GAP_LEGEND + H_LEGEND + PAD_BOTTOM
  yy <- function(v) total_h - v                     # layout px (top-down) -> plot y

  # is.finite(): a zero-case intervention has no dot but stays in (n) and the pool.
  pts <- per_intervention %>%
    mutate(nns = .data[[which_nns]]) %>%
    filter(is.finite(nns)) %>%
    inner_join(select(rows, variable, option_name, y_mid, col),
               by = c("variable", "option_name"))
  stopifnot(
    "a per-intervention value did not match a plotted category" =
      nrow(pts) == sum(is.finite(per_intervention[[which_nns]])),
    "a per-intervention value falls outside the plotted axis" =
      all(pts$nns >= X_MIN & pts$nns <= X_MAX)
  )

  grid_df <- tidyr::expand_grid(select(sec, section, rows_top, rows_bottom), x = BREAKS)
  # An undefined upper end runs to the panel edge and ends in an open arrowhead.
  bars <- rows %>%
    filter(count > 1, !is.na(Low), !is.na(High), High > Low) %>%
    mutate(x_bar_end = if_else(is.infinite(High), x_of(X_MAX), x_of(High)))
  bars_defined   <- filter(bars, is.finite(High))
  bars_undefined <- filter(bars, is.infinite(High))
  lab_gap <- 4.5                              # one space between the name and "(n=…)"

  g <- ggplot() +
    # gridlines, confined to their own section's rows
    geom_segment(data = grid_df,
                 aes(x = x_of(x), xend = x_of(x),
                     y = yy(rows_top), yend = yy(rows_bottom)),
                 colour = gridline, linewidth = lw(1), linetype = "dotted") +
    # 1 px rule under every row
    geom_segment(data = rows,
                 aes(x = PAD_SIDE, xend = PAD_SIDE + CONTENT_W,
                     y = yy(y_rule), yend = yy(y_rule)),
                 colour = row_rule, linewidth = lw(1)) +
    # section rule + header
    geom_segment(data = sec,
                 aes(x = PAD_SIDE, xend = PAD_SIDE + CONTENT_W,
                     y = yy(rule_y), yend = yy(rule_y), colour = col),
                 linewidth = lw(2.5)) +
    geom_text(data = sec, aes(x = PAD_SIDE, y = yy(text_y), label = letter, colour = col),
              hjust = 0, vjust = 0, fontface = "bold", size = tsz(16.5), family = fam) +
    geom_text(data = sec, aes(x = PAD_SIDE + 15, y = yy(text_y), label = section),
              hjust = 0, vjust = 0, fontface = "bold", size = tsz(16.5),
              family = fam, colour = ink) +
    # range line, then the real per-intervention values, then the pooled estimate
    geom_segment(data = bars_defined,
                 aes(x = x_of(Low), xend = x_bar_end, y = yy(y_mid), yend = yy(y_mid),
                     colour = col),
                 linewidth = lw(2), lineend = "round") +
    geom_segment(data = bars_undefined,
                 aes(x = x_of(Low), xend = x_bar_end, y = yy(y_mid), yend = yy(y_mid),
                     colour = col),
                 linewidth = lw(2), lineend = "butt",
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(px(9), "mm"), type = "open",
                               angle = 22, ends = "last")) +
    geom_point(data = pts, aes(x = x_of(nns), y = yy(y_mid), colour = col),
               alpha = 0.42, size = psz(7), stroke = 0) +
    geom_point(data = rows, aes(x = x_of(WeightedInvMean), y = yy(y_mid), colour = col,
                                size = psz(dia_px(n_non_missing))), stroke = 0) +
    # label column: name in ink, "(n=…)" in secondary, both right-aligned
    geom_text(data = rows, aes(x = x_lab, y = yy(y_mid), label = n_lab),
              hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = tsz(15.5), family = fam, colour = secondary) +
    geom_text(data = rows,
              aes(x = x_lab - str_w_px(n_lab, 15.5) - lab_gap, y = yy(y_mid),
                  label = option_name),
              hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = tsz(15.5), family = fam, colour = ink) +
    # estimate column
    geom_text(data = rows, aes(x = x_est, y = yy(y_mid), label = est_fig),
              hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5, size = tsz(15), family = fam, colour = ink) +
    annotate("text", x = x_est, y = yy(sec$text_y[1]), label = "NNS (range)",
             hjust = 0, vjust = 0, size = tsz(NOTE_PX), fontface = "bold",
             family = fam, colour = "#000000") +
    # axis
    annotate("text", x = x_of(BREAKS), y = yy(ticks_y),
             label = format(BREAKS, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE),
             hjust = 0.5, vjust = 1, size = tsz(14), family = fam, colour = muted) +
    annotate("text", x = x_plot0 + w_plot / 2, y = yy(title_y), label = x_title,
             hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5, size = tsz(15.5), fontface = "bold",
             family = fam, colour = ink) +
    scale_colour_identity() + scale_size_identity() +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, CARD_W), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, total_h), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
          plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA))

  # size legend: text, then one dot + number per n, laid out left to right and
  # centred over the plot column (12 px between items, 7 px dot -> number)
  leg_head <- "Interventions (n)"
  w_head <- str_w_px(leg_head, 14)
  w_num  <- str_w_px(as.character(LEGEND_N), 14)
  d      <- dia_px(LEGEND_N)
  item_w <- d + 7 + w_num
  leg_w  <- w_head + sum(item_w) + 12 * length(LEGEND_N)
  x0     <- x_plot0 + w_plot / 2 - leg_w / 2
  dot_x  <- x0 + w_head + cumsum(c(0, item_w[-length(item_w)])) + 12 * seq_along(LEGEND_N) + d / 2
  leg <- tibble(n = LEGEND_N, dot_x = dot_x, num_x = dot_x + d / 2 + 7, size = psz(d))

  g <- g +
    annotate("text", x = x0, y = yy(legend_y), label = leg_head,
             hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5, size = tsz(14), family = fam, colour = muted) +
    geom_point(data = leg, aes(x = dot_x, y = yy(legend_y), size = size),
               colour = legend_dot, stroke = 0) +
    geom_text(data = leg, aes(x = num_x, y = yy(legend_y), label = n),
              hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5, size = tsz(14), family = fam, colour = muted)

  list(plot = g, height_mm = total_h * mm_per_px, rows = rows, points = pts)
}

f_af    <- nns_figure("nns_af",    "Pooled NNS (all forms TB), log scale")
f_bplus <- nns_figure("nns_bplus", "Pooled NNS (bacteriologically confirmed TB), log scale",
                      x_limits = c(20, 5000), x_breaks = c(30, 100, 300, 1000, 3000))

p_af    <- f_af$plot
p_bplus <- f_bplus$plot

p_af
p_bplus

# 600 dpi PNG at print size: the submission copy.
save_figure <- function(plot, stem, width = 8, height = 7.5, units = "in") {
  ggsave(here("output", paste0(stem, "_600dpi.png")), plot = plot,
         width = width, height = height, units = units, dpi = 600)
}

save_figure(p_af, "Figure_pooled_nns_af",
            width = fig_w_mm, height = f_af$height_mm, units = "mm")
save_figure(p_bplus, "Figure_pooled_nns_bplus",
            width = fig_w_mm, height = f_bplus$height_mm, units = "mm")
```

## The screening cascade

The NNS factorises exactly into the three steps of the screening cascade, an identity that holds by construction:

$$
\underbrace{\frac{\text{screened}}{\text{cases}}}_{\text{NNS}}
=
\underbrace{\frac{\text{screened}}{\text{presumptive}}}_{\text{breadth of screen}}
\times
\underbrace{\frac{\text{presumptive}}{\text{tested}}}_{\text{testing coverage}}
\times
\underbrace{\frac{\text{tested}}{\text{cases}}}_{\text{diagnostic yield (NNT)}}
$$

The intermediate terms cancel, so the three factors multiply back to the NNS for a single intervention and, because each factor is a ratio of sums, for any group of interventions. A difference in NNS between two groups can therefore be attributed to the three steps in full and without a modelling assumption.

Breadth of screen is the number of people screened for every person classified as having presumptive TB, where a high value means a narrow screen that identified fewer people with presumptive TB. Testing coverage is the number of people classified presumptive for every person tested, so it sits at 1 where everyone flagged was tested. Diagnostic yield is the number needed to test (NNT). In the manuscript this decomposition is Supplementary S2 and the size gradient is Supplementary S3: most of the difference between strata was found in the breadth of screening, with testing coverage close to 1 and a narrow range of NNT, and breadth of screen was the only step that rose with the size of the intervention.

Everything below uses the all-forms case definition. Bacteriological confirmation changes only the third factor, because fewer cases pass that bar, so running the decomposition twice would repeat the first two columns unchanged. The B+ NNT is in the estimate tables above.

```{r}
#| label: cascade-terms
#| include: false

# Named once: legend keys, facet labels and column names.
stage_names <- c("Breadth of screen (screened per presumptive)",
                 "Testing coverage (presumptive per tested)",
                 "Diagnostic yield (tested per case, NNT)")

# count_ratio as in the calculation chunk, so the third term equals nnt_af.
master <- master %>%
  mutate(
    screen_per_presumptive = count_ratio(screened,    presumptive),
    presumptive_per_tested = count_ratio(presumptive, tested),
    tested_per_case        = count_ratio(tested,      tb_af)
  )

# Check the identity where every factor is finite (Inf * 0 is NaN).
identity_check <- master %>%
  filter(if_all(c(screen_per_presumptive, presumptive_per_tested,
                  tested_per_case, nns_af), is.finite))
stopifnot(
  "the three-factor decomposition does not reproduce the NNS" =
    isTRUE(all.equal(
      identity_check$screen_per_presumptive *
        identity_check$presumptive_per_tested *
        identity_check$tested_per_case,
      identity_check$nns_af
    ))
)

# cascade_set: all four cascade counts recorded, 61 of 67 (three of the 64 with a
# defined NNS have a blanked presumptive count). Zero-case interventions stay in.
# decomp_set: every factor finite, for the log-scale scatter only.
cascade_counts <- c("screened", "presumptive", "tested", "tb_af")

cascade_set <- master %>% filter(if_all(all_of(cascade_counts), ~ !is.na(.x)))
decomp_set  <- cascade_set %>% filter(presumptive > 0, tested > 0, tb_af > 0)

stopifnot(
  "the cascade set is not the 61 interventions with all four cascade counts" =
    nrow(cascade_set) == 61
)

# Ratios of summed counts, so the identity holds exactly.
pooled_stages <- function(d) {
  out <- tibble(
    n           = nrow(d),
    screened    = sum(d$screened),
    presumptive = sum(d$presumptive),
    tested      = sum(d$tested),
    cases       = sum(d$tb_af)
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      screen_per_presumptive = screened / presumptive,
      presumptive_per_tested = presumptive / tested,
      tested_per_case        = tested / cases,
      nns                    = screened / cases
    )
  stopifnot(
    "pooled factors do not multiply back to the pooled NNS" =
      isTRUE(all.equal(with(out, screen_per_presumptive *
                              presumptive_per_tested * tested_per_case),
                       out$nns))
  )
  out
}

# On the log scale the identity is additive.
log_factors <- decomp_set %>%
  transmute(
    intervention_id, project_code, screened,
    `Breadth of screen (screened per presumptive)` = log(screen_per_presumptive),
    `Testing coverage (presumptive per tested)`    = log(presumptive_per_tested),
    `Diagnostic yield (tested per case, NNT)`      = log(tested_per_case),
    total                                          = log(nns_af)
  )

stopifnot(
  "log factors do not sum to log NNS" =
    isTRUE(all.equal(rowSums(as.matrix(log_factors[stage_names])), log_factors$total))
)
```

```{r}
#| label: cascade-strata
#| include: false

# Purpose-built contrasts; the forest-plot combination labels fragment into
# n = 1 rows. %in% 1 so an unrecorded flag reads as not used.
membership <- cascade_set %>%
  mutate(
    tertile = ntile(screened, 3),
    any_cxr = screening_methods_cxr %in% 1 | screening_methods_cxr_ai %in% 1,

    `1. Overall|All interventions`             = TRUE,
    `2. Screening approach|Mass screening`     = screening_stage_mass_screening %in% 1,
    `2. Screening approach|Not mass screening` = !screening_stage_mass_screening %in% 1,
    `3. Screening tool|Any chest X-ray`        = any_cxr,
    `3. Screening tool|No chest X-ray`         = !any_cxr,
    `4. Volume screened|Largest third`         = tertile == 3,
    `4. Volume screened|Middle third`          = tertile == 2,
    `4. Volume screened|Smallest third`        = tertile == 1
  )

stratum_cols <- str_subset(names(membership), fixed("|"))

cascade_strata <- map_dfr(stratum_cols, function(col) {
  pooled_stages(filter(membership, .data[[col]])) %>%
    mutate(stratum = col, .before = 1)
}) %>%
  separate_wider_delim(stratum, "|", names = c("section", "label")) %>%
  # The numeric prefix fixes the order; drop it for display, keep it as levels.
  mutate(section = fct_inorder(str_remove(section, "^\\d+\\. ")),
         label   = fct_inorder(label)) %>%
  arrange(section, label)

stopifnot(
  "a stratum is empty" = all(cascade_strata$n > 0),
  "the complementary pairs do not partition the 61" =
    all(c(sum(cascade_strata$n[cascade_strata$section == "Screening approach"]),
          sum(cascade_strata$n[cascade_strata$section == "Screening tool"]),
          sum(cascade_strata$n[cascade_strata$section == "Volume screened"])) == 61)
)
```

```{r}
#| label: cascade-figure-setup
#| include: false

# Same face and ink as the forest plots and the map; the hues carry the steps.
panel_bg  <- "#FDFCFA"
stage_pal <- c("#8E2F3C", "#A97B23", "#1F6E73")   # maroon, gold, peacock
names(stage_pal) <- stage_names

theme_cascade <- function(base_size = 9) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size, base_family = fam) +
    theme(
      plot.background   = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.background  = element_rect(fill = panel_bg, colour = NA),
      panel.grid.minor  = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = gridline, linewidth = 0.25),
      axis.text         = element_text(colour = ink),
      axis.title        = element_text(colour = muted, size = rel(0.95)),
      strip.text        = element_text(colour = ink, face = "bold", hjust = 0,
                                       size = rel(0.95)),
      # Align title and caption to the plot, not the panel.
      plot.title.position   = "plot",
      plot.caption.position = "plot",
      plot.title        = element_text(colour = ink, face = "bold", size = rel(1.25)),
      plot.subtitle     = element_text(colour = muted, size = rel(0.95), lineheight = 1.2),
      plot.caption      = element_text(colour = muted, size = rel(0.8), hjust = 0,
                                       lineheight = 1.25),
      legend.position   = "top",
      legend.title      = element_blank(),
      legend.text       = element_text(colour = ink)
    )
}
```

### Supplementary S2. Decomposition of the number needed to screen into the screening cascade

The identity is multiplicative, so the figure is a waterfall. The x axis is the running product from one person screened to the NNS, and the length of a segment is that step's multiplicative weight.

The strata are purpose-built contrasts: mass screening or not, any chest X-ray against no chest X-ray, and tertiles of the number screened. The combination labels used for the forest plots above describe what projects did, but they fragment into rows of n = 1 and a decomposition cannot use them.

**Supplementary S2, `Figure_cascade_waterfall`: Decomposition of the number needed to screen into the screening cascade.** The NNS (All forms of TB, 61 interventions with a complete cascade) is the product of three steps shown on the figure. The x-axis is logarithmic so the length of each segment is that step's multiplicative weight. Bold figures at the right are the NNS for the stratum.

Writes `Figure_cascade_waterfall` to `output/`.

```{r}
#| label: figure-cascade-waterfall
#| include: true
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 7.5
#| fig-height: 4.2

# Waterfall on a log axis: each step's length is its log contribution, and the
# middle step can run backwards. fct_inorder keeps the tertile order.
wf_rows <- cascade_strata %>%
  mutate(row_label = fct_inorder(sprintf("%s (n=%d)", label, n)))

wf <- wf_rows %>%
  transmute(
    section, row_label, nns,
    c1 = screen_per_presumptive,
    c2 = screen_per_presumptive * presumptive_per_tested,
    c3 = screen_per_presumptive * presumptive_per_tested * tested_per_case
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(c1, c2, c3), names_to = "step", values_to = "cum_end") %>%
  group_by(section, row_label) %>%
  mutate(cum_start = lag(cum_end, default = 1)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    stage = factor(recode(step, c1 = stage_names[1], c2 = stage_names[2],
                          c3 = stage_names[3]), levels = stage_names),
    x_start = log10(cum_start),
    x_end   = log10(cum_end)
  )

stopifnot(
  "a waterfall row does not end at its stratum NNS" =
    isTRUE(all.equal(
      wf %>% filter(step == "c3") %>% pull(cum_end),
      wf %>% filter(step == "c3") %>% pull(nns)
    ))
)

X_MAX <- log10(1200)                       # room for the estimate column
x_breaks <- c(1, 3, 10, 30, 100, 300)

# In-bar multipliers on the first and third steps only; the middle is too short.
wf_labels <- wf %>%
  filter(step %in% c("c1", "c3")) %>%
  mutate(x_mid = (x_start + x_end) / 2,
         lab   = sprintf("×%.1f", cum_end / cum_start))

p_waterfall <- ggplot(wf, aes(y = row_label)) +
  geom_linerange(data = filter(wf, step != "c2"),
                 aes(xmin = x_start, xmax = x_end, colour = stage),
                 linewidth = 5.5) +
  # Thinner and on top, so a backwards step stays visible.
  geom_linerange(data = filter(wf, step == "c2"),
                 aes(xmin = x_start, xmax = x_end, colour = stage),
                 linewidth = 2.2) +
  geom_text(data = wf_labels, aes(x = x_mid, label = lab),
            colour = "white", family = fam, size = 2.5, fontface = "bold") +
  geom_text(data = wf_rows, aes(x = X_MAX, label = disp_range(nns)),
            hjust = 1, colour = ink, family = fam, size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(section), scales = "free_y", space = "free_y",
             switch = "y",
             labeller = as_labeller(function(x) str_wrap(x, 11))) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    name   = "Running product, from 1 person screened to the number needed to screen (log scale)",
    breaks = log10(x_breaks), labels = x_breaks,
    limits = c(0, X_MAX), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.005, 0))
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(name = NULL, limits = rev) +
  # Wrapped so the three keys fit at 190 mm.
  scale_colour_manual(values = stage_pal, drop = FALSE,
                      labels = function(x) str_wrap(x, 26)) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linewidth = 3), nrow = 1)) +
  theme_cascade() +
  # Title and caption live in the document; the colour key stays with the plot.
  theme(strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
        strip.placement   = "outside",
        legend.position   = "bottom",
        legend.text       = element_text(colour = ink, size = rel(0.78)))

p_waterfall

save_figure(p_waterfall, "Figure_cascade_waterfall",
            width = 190, height = 107, units = "mm")
```

### Supplementary S3. Relationship of size of the projects and outcomes

One panel per step, on a shared y axis so that the three can be compared by eye and not only by their slopes.

**Supplementary S3, `Figure_cascade_gradient`: Relationship of size of the projects and outcomes.** Each point is one intervention. Larger interventions classified a much smaller share of those screened as presumptive, while their yield among the people they tested was flat. The figure shows 58 of the 61 interventions with a complete cascade; the three omitted screened people and found no one with TB, so their NNT is undefined. Lines are from the ordinary least squares regression shown to convey direction.

Writes `Figure_cascade_gradient` to `output/`.

```{r}
#| label: figure-cascade-gradient
#| include: true
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 2.8

grad_long <- log_factors %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(stage_names), names_to = "stage", values_to = "log_ratio") %>%
  mutate(stage = factor(stage, levels = stage_names))

p_gradient <- ggplot(grad_long, aes(x = screened, y = exp(log_ratio))) +
  geom_smooth(aes(colour = stage), method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE,
              linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = stage), alpha = 0.65, size = 1.6, stroke = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~stage, nrow = 1,
             labeller = as_labeller(function(x) str_wrap(x, 30))) +
  scale_x_log10(name = "People screened by the intervention",
                labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())) +
  scale_y_log10(name = "Ratio at this step",
                breaks = c(1, 3, 10, 30, 100, 300),
                labels = c(1, 3, 10, 30, 100, 300)) +
  annotation_logticks(sides = "bl", colour = gridline, size = 0.25,
                      short = unit(0.4, "mm"), mid = unit(0.8, "mm"),
                      long = unit(1.2, "mm")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = stage_pal, guide = "none") +
  theme_cascade() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = gridline, linewidth = 0.25))

p_gradient

save_figure(p_gradient, "Figure_cascade_gradient",
            width = 190, height = 70, units = "mm")
```
